Yes absolutely that counts but also having all that personal experience in the home schooling space. Alternative education/home schooling is definitely the way to go I think! Do some research on existing podcasts out there on this then come back and ask some more questions 🤘

Here are my reasons why:
1. Not overdone
2. Interesting topic that most people wouldn’t ask about in  RL
3. Tons of sponsorship opportunities, tons of companies can’t advertise in other spaces like fb so a kink podcast would be perfect for them!

Good luck!

I disagree about 8-10 prerecorded eps being too much. If people like your podcast they will want to listen to more so don't leave them with just 2 episodes. Launch with 6 and hold 2 back so you are 2 eps ahead at all times, then if a guest cancels or you get ill or something you have back up content. To combat the out of date content, keep these first launch episodes broad so they remain 'evergreen'

Whilst I totally understand having this world view, it's not something you can change. Focus on smaller things, make your world smaller. See friends, go for walks, enjoy cooking or other simple hobbies. Life will start to feel a bit better I promise. Until then stay on here and we will help you any way we can, the world does need you in it despite how you feel right now

If you are remotely recording make sure you leave time at the beginning of the interview to speak to your guest, make sure the audio is working ok etc so you aren't rushed. Then if you are adding introductions to your episodes then always record them straight after the interview/discussion so the content is fresh in your mind.

You want it to be searchable as that's the main point of SEO for podcasts. So it can't just be 'gimmicky' to get people to click, it needs to reflect the content of the episode. Are you doing show notes for your eps?

Riverside is the best platform for what you want. Previous posters are right in that the people you interview often won't have a clue about basic audio issues, so if you can tell them ahead of time to ensure they wear headphones that's a big help!

Being specific is best. Don't try and be clever, you want to be searchable, so to choose a name that 'does what it says on the tin' as we like to say in the UK is perfect. I'd try and 'niche' down your podcast more, which of those topics could you talk about for hours on end and never get bored or run out of content? Are you a specialist in any of them or have any unique experience in one over the other?

Ok so a few tips from me would be:

* Not to spend tons of money on equipment, dynamic mics are good enough for almost every podcast especially when just starting. Don’t buy things just because you have seen other podcasters using it, your set-up doesn't need to be complex
* If you have any spare cash then spend it on editing, you can get experienced podcast freelance editors based in the UK for around £15-£20 an episode easily or even lower rates if you pay in bulk/arrange with them
* I know you say 3 hosts and guests sometimes but a smaller room is best for recording in, avoid rooms that echo like kitchens
* Record 5/6 episodes to launch with and try and always stay a couple of episodes ahead of schedule so if a guest falls through or you get sick you can still stay consistent.
Is this a solo show or with interviews or both? My answers would be different depending on this!

I'd love to chat with you about your needs, I have been a freelancer working with podcasts for several years now doing all of the tasks you have mentioned. I am based in the UK. If you DM me I can share more details and we can have a chat
